comfortable adjective

of a seat, a bed, clothes, a journey

also comfortably, uncomfortable, comfy, cosy, make yourself comfortable, cozy

classical

Liv. 22.2.2 (Lewis & Short): longius cēterum commodius iter
Ov. F. 2.288 (Lewis & Short): commoda vestis, of clothes for running
Traupman 294: commodus, comfortable
Traupman 294
Traupman 298

commodus, commoda, commodum

adjective: with the dative or ad of what it suits, declension

comfortable, convenient, suitable

What fits its use well: a road, winter quarters, a garment for running. Of a person it means obliging, pleasant; commodum est is “it suits, it is convenient” (Lewis & Short). The opposite is incommodus, and the adverbs commodē, incommodē are “comfortably, uncomfortably”.

Other words

  • mollis, molle — soft

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical

    For a bed, a cushion or a seat, Latin says it is soft. Of people it is gentle, tender, and also weak or effeminate (Lewis & Short).

  • rogō ut vōbīs suāviter sit — make yourselves comfortable

    phrase · also used · modern · Traupman 95, 294

    Traupman’s host’s phrase; suāviter is classical, “pleasantly”, but this use of it with esse was not found in Cicero’s letters, Plautus or Terence.

Examples

  • Actiō māluimus iter facere pedibus quī incommodissimē nāvigāssēmus

    from Actium we preferred to travel on foot, after a most uncomfortable voyageCic. Att. 5.9.1

  • pr. Īdūs Oct. Athēnās vēnimus, cum sānē adversīs ventīs ūsī essēmus tardēque et incommodē nāvigāssēmus

    we reached Athens on 14 October, after a voyage with contrary winds, slow and uncomfortableCic. Fam. 14.5.1

  • modo fac, id quod est hūmānitātis tuae, nē quid aliud cūrēs hōc tempore nisi ut quam commodissimē convalēscās

    only see to it, as your good sense will, that for now you think of nothing but getting well as comfortably as you canCic. Fam. 16.11.1

See also comfortable, soft, sofa.
